title: Demystifying the adoption of behavior-driven development in open source projects
authors: Zampetti, F.; Di Sorbo, A.; Visaggio, C.A.; Canfora, G.; Di Penta, M.
supporting_sentence: In about 37% of the cases, we found a co-evolution between scenarios/fixtures and production code.
relevance: Closest prior work: large-scale BDD framework adoption in OSS plus scenario/production co-evolution; no mutation analysis, no oracle-strength measurement.

title: An Exploratory Study on the Usage of Gherkin Features in Open-Source Projects
authors: Chandorkar, A.; Patkar, N.; Di Sorbo, A.; Nierstrasz, O.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis Evolution and Reengineering (SANER)
supporting_sentence: To fill this gap, we analyzed the content of 1,572 spec files extracted from 23 open-source projects.
relevance: Empirical characterisation of Gherkin feature usage in public repos; structural metrics of scenario files, no execution or oracle strength.

title: Maintaining behaviour driven development specifications: Challenges and opportunities
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Embury, S.M.; Konstantinou, N.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis Evolution and Reengineering (SANER)
supporting_sentence: We surveyed 75 BDD practitioners from 26 countries to understand the extent of BDD use, its benefits and challenges, and specifically the challenges of maintaining BDD specifications
relevance: Practitioner survey establishing BDD specification maintenance pain; motivates drift but reports no measurements on suites.

title: Characterising the Quality of Behaviour Driven Development Specifications
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Embury, S.M.; Konstantinou, N.
venue: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
supporting_sentence: Despite much discussion amongst practitioners and in the blogosphere, as yet no formal definition of what makes for a high quality BDD suite has been given.
relevance: Defines BDD suite quality principles from a practitioner survey; quality judged by criteria, never by fault-detection measurement.

title: Behaviour driven development: A systematic mapping study
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: maps 166 BDD papers (2006-2021) and reports an acute shortage of metrics for measuring aspects of BDD specifications and of the processes producing them
relevance: Umbrella map of BDD research; zero occurrences of mutation, fault detection, step definition or longitudinal, evidencing our gap.

title: Behavior Driven Development: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Farooq, M.S.; Omer, U.; Ramzan, A.; Rasheed, M.A.; Atal, Z.
supporting_sentence: This study presents a review of the state-of-the-art BDD by synthesizing the recent advancements in its uses and applications.
relevance: Second secondary study of BDD impact on process and product quality; no suite-level fault-detection measurement.

title: How to Evaluate BDD Scenarios' Quality?
authors: Oliveira, G.; Marczak, S.; Moralles, C.
venue: Proceedings of the XXXIII Brazilian Symposium on Software Engineering (SBES)
supporting_sentence: To address this lack of guidance, we define a set of quality attributes and propose a question-based checklist to assist BDD scenarios' quality evaluations.
relevance: Defines scenario quality attributes from 18 practitioner interviews; quality is checklist-based, not measured by mutant detection.

title: On the Empirical Evaluation of BDD Scenarios Quality: Preliminary Findings of an Empirical Study
venue: IEEE International Requirements Engineering Conference Workshops (REW)
supporting_sentence: On this research design paper, we describe a study designed to understand how known quality attributes from other types of requirements specifications (like use cases or user stories) can be used with BDD scenarios.
relevance: Earliest stage of the Oliveira/Marczak scenario-quality line; research design plus novice-evaluator findings, no execution-based measure.

title: On the Characterization of Behavior-Driven Development Adoption Benefits: A Multiple Case Study
authors: Couto, T.; Marczak, S.; Callegari, D.; Móra, M.; Gomes, F.
venue: Proceedings of the XXI Brazilian Symposium on Software Quality (SBQS)
supporting_sentence: Although the claims that BDD adoption improves product and software processes, there is still no consolidated evidence about its benefits nor have we found quality indicators to measure them.
relevance: Multiple case study of BDD benefits in novice teams; confirms absence of indicators to measure BDD benefits, supporting measurement gap.

title: Assertions are strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 10th Joint Meeting on Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE)
supporting_sentence: We find that the number of assertions in a test suite strongly correlates with its effectiveness, and this factor directly influences the relation
relevance: Core mechanism evidence: assertions drive mutant-detected effectiveness; our step-definition assertion metric is its transfer to BDD.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Assertions as Oracles
venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Testing Verification and Validation (ICST)
supporting_sentence: In this paper, we report the results of one such experiment in which we exercise seven core Java classes and two sample programs with branch-adequate, input only(i.e., no oracle) test suites and collect the failures observed by different oracles.
relevance: Shows oracle-free suites detect almost nothing even when branch-adequate; direct precedent for measuring unassertive BDD steps.

title: On Adequacy of Assertions in Automated Test Suites: An Empirical Investigation
venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Testing Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
supporting_sentence: The paper reports an empirical study on the Inadequate-Assertion (IA) problem in the context of automated test suites developed for open-source projects.
relevance: Names and measures the inadequate-assertion problem in OSS suites using mutation analysis; template for our vacuous-step construct.

title: An empirical study on the evolution of test smell
venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 42nd International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings (ICSE-C)
supporting_sentence: Our result shows that Assertion Roulette, Conditional Test Logic and Unknown tests have a high rate of churns, the feature addition and improvement motivate refactoring, but test smell persists, implicating sub-optimal practice.
relevance: Longitudinal test-smell persistence, including Assertion Roulette (multiple assertions per test); closest erosion-of-quality precedent outside BDD.

title: Revisiting the Identification of the Co-evolution of Production and Test Code
authors: Sun, W.; Yan, M.; Liu, Z.; Xia, X.; Lei, Y.; Lo, D.
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
supporting_sentence: Many software processes advocate that the test code should co-evolve with the production code.
relevance: Methodological warning: mined production-test co-evolution samples are noisy; we must not reuse naive co-evolution heuristics for BDD history.

title: Mutta: a novel tool for E2E web mutation testing
authors: Leotta, M.; Paparella, D.; Ricca, F.
supporting_sentence: In detail, Mutta has been executed on two web applications, each equipped with different test suites to compare assertions with differential testing.
relevance: Closest mutation-based evaluation of acceptance-style web suites; two apps, not Gherkin, not domain-layer, not longitudinal.

title: Supporting refactoring of BDD specifications—An empirical study
authors: Irshad, M.; Börstler, J.; Petersen, K.
supporting_sentence: Although refactoring is a crucial activity of BDD, little research is available on the topic.
relevance: Industrial action research on detecting BDD refactoring candidates via similarity; measures duplication, never fault detection.

title: Smells in system user interactive tests
authors: Rwemalika, R.; Habchi, S.; Papadakis, M.; Le Traon, Y.; Brasseur, M.C.
supporting_sentence: We also conduct an empirical analysis to assess the diffuseness and removal of these smells in 48 industrial repositories and 12 open-source projects.
relevance: Largest smell+removal study for system-level interactive tests (35 smells, 60 repos); BDD-adjacent but not Gherkin-scoped and no oracle strength.
